Class VisionPoseFilter

java.lang.Object
yall.filter.VisionPoseFilter
public class VisionPoseFilter extends Object
Decides which vision pose estimates to trust, and how much.

Each check is set with its withX method. Pass null to turn the check off: 

new VisionPoseFilter()
    .withMaxAmbiguity(0.15)       // tighter than the default
    .withMaxTilt(Degrees.of(10))  // on; off by default
    .withMaxYawRate(null);        // off

A new filter starts with these checks:

Checks and their defaults
CheckDefaultRejects an estimate when
Field boundsOn, 0.5 m margin the robot would be off the field
HeightOn, 0.5 m the robot would be floating above or sunk below the floor
TiltOff the robot would be rolled or pitched further than the limit
AmbiguityOn, 0.2 a single-tag estimate is too ambiguous
Tag countOn, 1 tag too few tags were used
Tag distance On, 4 m for one tag, 8 m for severalthe tags are too far away
Yaw rateOn, 720 °/s the robot was spinning too fast, which blurs the image (needs VisionCamera.setRobotOrientation(Rotation3d, AngularVelocity))
AgeOn, 0.5 s the image is too old, or claims to be from the future
Pose jumpOff the estimate is too far from the robot's current pose

Add your own checks with withCustomCheck(String, Predicate). Each has a name, which is the rejection reason and the name its rejections are counted under in PoseFilterStats.

Estimates that used no tags are always rejected.

Accepted estimates get standard deviations that grow with the square of the tag distance: base * (1 + distance² / distanceDivisor), with a smaller base for multi-tag estimates. See withStdDevs(Matrix, Matrix, double).

      Returns:
      This filter, for chaining.

    • withMaxDistanceFromPose

      public VisionPoseFilter withMaxDistanceFromPose(Supplier<Pose2d> currentPose, Distance maxDistance)
      Rejects estimates further than the limit from the robot's current pose. Turn this on only once the robot knows where it is, or vision can never correct a bad starting pose.
      Parameters:
      currentPose - Supplies the robot's current pose, usually from the drivetrain's pose estimator. null turns the check off.
      maxDistance - Largest accepted distance from the current pose. null turns the check off.
      Returns:
      This filter, for chaining.

    • withCustomCheck

      public VisionPoseFilter withCustomCheck(String name, Predicate<VisionPoseEstimate> accepts)
      Adds a check of your own, run after the built-in ones. Its name is the rejection reason, and PoseFilterStats counts its rejections under that name. 
      filter.withCustomCheck("not in our half", e -> e.pose().getX() < 8.27);
      Parameters:
      name - Name of the check, shown as the rejection reason. Must not be empty. A check with the same name is replaced.
      accepts - Returns true to accept an estimate. null removes the check.
      Returns:
      This filter, for chaining.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the name is null or blank.

    • withStdDevs

      public VisionPoseFilter withStdDevs(Matrix<N3,N1> singleTagBase, Matrix<N3,N1> multiTagBase, double distanceDivisor)
      Sets how standard deviations are computed for accepted estimates: base * (1 + d² / distanceDivisor), where d is the average tag distance in meters. A smaller divisor makes distant tags count for less.

      This filter, for chaining.

    • withStdDevScale

      public VisionPoseFilter withStdDevScale(DoubleSupplier xyScaleSupplier)
      Applies a dynamic multiplier to accepted X/Y standard deviations (for example, switching between normal driving, close-in alignment, and post-bump relocalization snap modes).

    • withHighTagCountBoost

      public VisionPoseFilter withHighTagCountBoost(Integer minTags, Double xyScale)
      Applies an extra X/Y standard deviation multiplier when an estimate sees at least minTags AprilTags (for example, trusting a 3+ tag shooter-camera solve more tightly).
      Parameters:
      minTags - Fewest tags required for the boost (must be >= 2). null turns the boost off.
      xyScale - Positive multiplier applied to X and Y standard deviations (e.g. 0.35). null turns the boost off.
      Returns:
      This filter, for chaining.

    • withPreEnableAlignment

      public VisionPoseFilter withPreEnableAlignment(BooleanSupplier isEnabled, Integer minPreEnableTags, Angle preEnableThetaStdDev)
      Enables pre-enable (disabled) field alignment: while isEnabled returns false, the pose-jump gate is bypassed so vision can snap to the field from an unknown starting pose, at least minPreEnableTags tags are required, and heading uses preEnableThetaStdDev so multi-tag solves can align the gyro before the match starts.
      Parameters:
      isEnabled - Supplies whether the robot is currently enabled (e.g. DriverStation::isEnabled). null turns pre-enable alignment off.
      minPreEnableTags - Fewest tags required while disabled (must be >= 1). null defaults to 2.
      preEnableThetaStdDev - Heading standard deviation while disabled. null defaults to 2 deg.
      Returns:
      This filter, for chaining.
